subject: physics
question_text: What is the relation between the pressure of a gas and the average kinetic energy of a molecule?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya IPE Study Material for Jr. Students 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 13 Very Short Answer Question 8 (printed p.137). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: P = ⅔n(½mv̄²), with n = N/V the number density and ½mv̄² the average kinetic energy of one molecule, follows from PV = ⅔N(½mv̄²) divided by V; pressure is directly proportional to the average kinetic energy of a molecule, matching NCERT Class-11 Chapter 13. This card answers for the kinetic energy of ONE molecule — the companion question about the gas's total internal energy is a separate card.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The relation

steps.margin_note: First mark. Write P = ⅔n(½mv̄²) and name n as the number of molecules per unit volume.
steps.why: Kinetic theory gives P = ⅓nmv̄² = ⅔n(½mv̄²). Here ½mv̄² is the average kinetic energy of one molecule, and n is how many such molecules occupy each unit of volume, so the formula links pressure to a single molecule's energy through the number density.
common_mistakes: Writing P = ⅔(½mv̄²) and leaving out n — without n the units do not even work out to pressure.
Confusing n, the number per unit volume, with N, the total number of molecules.

recall.must_convey: That P equals two thirds n times half m v bar squared, where n is the number of molecules per unit volume and half m v bar squared is the average kinetic energy of one molecule.
accept: P equals two thirds n half m v squared

steps.memory_tip: n counts molecules per unit volume; ½mv̄² is what one of them carries.

steps.margin_note: Second mark. State that pressure is directly proportional to the average kinetic energy of a molecule.
steps.why: In P = ⅔n(½mv̄²), n stays fixed for a given gas sample of fixed volume, so P rises and falls exactly as ½mv̄² does — a faster-moving molecule pushes harder on the wall every time it collides with it.
common_mistakes: Saying the pressure depends only on the number of molecules, leaving out that it also depends on how energetic each one is.
Stating the proportionality without naming which quantity, ½mv̄², the pressure is proportional to.

recall.must_convey: That the pressure of a gas is directly proportional to the average kinetic energy of a molecule.
accept: pressure proportional to average kinetic energy
directly proportional to kinetic energy of a molecule

steps.memory_tip: More energetic molecules push harder — pressure tracks the average kinetic energy of one molecule.

insider_note: This question asks about the kinetic energy of one molecule, not the gas's total internal energy — keep n and ½mv̄² as separate factors in both steps.
